options: carbohydrates that speed up digestion only
living cells that make reactions faster
proteins that function as biological catalysts
fats that are used up in metabolic reactions
questions.why: Enzymes are proteins involved in all metabolic reactions, acting as biological catalysts.

questions.q: Why does an enzyme stop working at 70 °C?
options: The active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits.
The enzyme has been killed by the heat.
The molecules move too slowly to collide.
The substrate becomes complementary to the product.
questions.why: High temperature denatures the enzyme: the active site shape changes permanently.

questions.q: Why does the rate of an enzyme reaction increase from 20 °C to 35 °C?
options: The active site becomes a better shape.
Molecules have more kinetic energy, so more frequent effective collisions.
questions.why: Below the optimum, more kinetic energy gives more enzyme–substrate collisions per second.

questions.q: Explain why an enzyme acts on only one type of substrate.
questions.model: The active site has a shape that is complementary to the substrate, so only that substrate fits and forms an enzyme–substrate complex.
points: only that substrate fits / forms an enzyme–substrate complex
